hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Oceania, continent between the Indian Ocean and the South Pacific Ocean || mostly low plateau with deserts; fertile plain in southeast || world's smallest continent but sixth-largest country; the largest country in Oceania, the largest country entirely in the Southern Hemisphere, and the largest country without land borders the Great Dividing Range that runs along eastern Australia is that continent’s longest mountain range and the third-longest land-based range in the world; the term "Great Dividing Range" refers to the fact that the mountains form a watershed crest from which all of the rivers of eastern Australia flow – east, west, north, and south Australia is the only continent without glaciers; it is the driest inhabited continent on earth; Perth on the west coast is home to the invigorating sea breeze known as the "Fremantle Doctor," one of the most consistent winds in the world; Australia hosts 10% of the world's biodiversity, and a great number of its flora and fauna exist nowhere else in the world || Resources: alumina, coal, iron ore, copper, lithium, tin, gold, silver, uranium, nickel, tungsten, rare earth elements, mineral sands, lead, zinc, diamonds, opals, natural gas, petroleum || Exports: iron ore, coal, natural gas, gold, minerals (2023)

climate.excerpt: generally arid to semiarid; temperate in south and east; tropical in north || cyclones along the coast; severe droughts; forest fires volcanism: volcanic activity on Heard and McDonald Islands

economy.excerpt: high-income and globally integrated economy; strong mining, manufacturing, and service sectors driving slow but steady growth; net exporter, driven by commodities to East Asian trade partners; weak productivity and aging population straining labor force participation || Exports: iron ore, coal, natural gas, gold, minerals (2023) || Industries: mining, industrial and transportation equipment, food processing, chemicals, steel
